title: CI-10 budget: count the whole dist or the installable plugin?
context: REQUIREMENTS CI-10 says the budget fails when dist/ is over 5 MB or 300 files, and spec AC-4 assumes the clean dist is under 300. But since PLG-12 (resolved decision D-01M4855FPAJB26APSF0R6H91WQ) the built dist carries the combined plugin (94 files) PLUS three per-host branches (claude, chatgpt, codex) at 94 files each, so the whole dist is 378 files and about 1.5 MB. A check that measures the whole dist tree therefore FAILS on the clean tree (378 over 300), turning CI permanently red; a single installable plugin is only 94 files, well under budget. The 300-file threshold predates the PLG-12 branch multiplication. How should check_budget (CI-10) count files so the budget guards real plugin size without a vacuous or permanent-red gate?

options.label: Measure the largest single installable unit (the combined plugin and each host branch) and apply 5 MB / 300 files to that; the whole-dist raw total is reported for visibility. Current max is 94 files, so it passes. Matches what a user actually installs.
Keep measuring the whole dist tree but raise the file threshold to fit the per-host branches (for example 600 files), keeping the 5 MB size cap.
Measure the whole dist against the literal 5 MB / 300 files as written in REQUIREMENTS; this fails now at 378 files and requires reducing shipped content or the number of branches.

rationale: Budget is a per-install limit; measure the largest single installable unit (94 files, under 300/5MB), report whole-dist total for visibility. 300/5MB predates per-host branching (PLG-12).
